    58  /**
    59   * htmlErrMemory:
    60   * @ctxt:  an HTML parser context
    61   * @extra:  extra information
    62   *
    63   * Handle a redefinition of attribute error
    64   */
    65  static void
    66  htmlErrMemory(xmlParserCtxtPtr ctxt, const char *extra)
    67  {
    68      if ((ctxt != NULL) && (ctxt->disableSAX != 0) &&
    69          (ctxt->instate == XML_PARSER_EOF))
    70          return;
    71      if (ctxt != NULL) {
    72          ctxt->errNo = XML_ERR_NO_MEMORY;
    73          ctxt->instate = XML_PARSER_EOF;
    74          ctxt->disableSAX = 1;
    75      }
    76      if (extra)
    77          __xmlRaiseError(NULL, NULL, NULL, ctxt, NULL, XML_FROM_PARSER,
    78                          XML_ERR_NO_MEMORY, XML_ERR_FATAL, NULL, 0, extra,
    79                          NULL, NULL, 0, 0,
    80                          "Memory allocation failed : %s\n", extra);
    81      else
    82          __xmlRaiseError(NULL, NULL, NULL, ctxt, NULL, XML_FROM_PARSER,
    83                          XML_ERR_NO_MEMORY, XML_ERR_FATAL, NULL, 0, NULL,
    84                          NULL, NULL, 0, 0, "Memory allocation failed\n");
    85  }

    99               const char *msg, const xmlChar *str1, const xmlChar *str2)

   104      if (ctxt != NULL)

   107                      XML_ERR_ERROR, NULL, 0,
   108                      (const char *) str1, (const char *) str2,
   109                      NULL, 0, 0,
   110                      msg, str1, str2);
   111      if (ctxt != NULL)
   112          ctxt->wellFormed = 0;
   113  }

   146  /**
   147   * htmlnamePush:
   148   * @ctxt:  an HTML parser context
   149   * @value:  the element name
   150   *
   151   * Pushes a new element name on top of the name stack
   152   *
   153   * Returns -1 in case of error, the index in the stack otherwise
   154   */
   155  static int
   156  htmlnamePush(htmlParserCtxtPtr ctxt, const xmlChar * value)
   157  {
   158      if ((ctxt->html < 3) && (xmlStrEqual(value, BAD_CAST "head")))
   159          ctxt->html = 3;
   160      if ((ctxt->html < 10) && (xmlStrEqual(value, BAD_CAST "body")))
   161          ctxt->html = 10;
   162      if (ctxt->nameNr >= ctxt->nameMax) {
   163          size_t newSize = ctxt->nameMax * 2;
   164          const xmlChar **tmp;
   165
   166          tmp = xmlRealloc((xmlChar **) ctxt->nameTab,
   167                           newSize * sizeof(ctxt->nameTab[0]));
   168          if (tmp == NULL) {
   169              htmlErrMemory(ctxt, NULL);
   170              return (-1);
   171          }
   172          ctxt->nameTab = tmp;
   173          ctxt->nameMax = newSize;
   174      }
   175      ctxt->nameTab[ctxt->nameNr] = value;
   176      ctxt->name = value;
   177      return (ctxt->nameNr++);
   178  }
   179  /**

   203      return (ret);

    40  /*
    41   * Macros for accessing the content. Those should be used only by the parser,
    42   * and not exported.
    43   *
    44   * Dirty macros, i.e. one need to make assumption on the context to use them
    45   *
    46   *   CUR_PTR return the current pointer to the xmlChar to be parsed.
    47   *   CUR     returns the current xmlChar value, i.e. a 8 bit value if compiled
    48   *           in ISO-Latin or UTF-8, and the current 16 bit value if compiled
    49   *           in UNICODE mode. This should be used internally by the parser
    50   *           only to compare to ASCII values otherwise it would break when
    51   *           running with UTF-8 encoding.
    52   *   NXT(n)  returns the n'th next xmlChar. Same as CUR is should be used only
    53   *           to compare on ASCII based substring.
    54   *   UPP(n)  returns the n'th next xmlChar converted to uppercase. Same as CUR
    55   *           it should be used only to compare on ASCII based substring.
    56   *   SKIP(n) Skip n xmlChar, and must also be used only to skip ASCII defined
    57   *           strings without newlines within the parser.
    58   *
    59   * Clean macros, not dependent of an ASCII context, expect UTF-8 encoding
    60   *
    61   *   NEXT    Skip to the next character, this does the proper decoding
    62   *           in UTF-8 mode. It also pop-up unfinished entities on the fly.
    63   *   NEXTL(l) Skip the current unicode character of l xmlChars long.
